About

Who I am

I’m Aindrila Das — a Business Process Trainer at Accenture and a community builder who believes education and dignity should reach every child.

Alongside professional work, I’ve volunteered with NGOs focused on libraries, donations, and fundraising for underprivileged children — including COVID-19 book and relief campaigns.

This page showcases that contribution honestly: clear about my volunteer role, concrete about published organizational reach, framed carefully so organizational reach stays distinct from personal contribution.

My work

My contributions

Three ways I’ve shown up — in my own voice, with organizational context for scale, without inventing personal KPIs or rupee totals.

Libraries

I helped set up and support libraries so children in underserved communities could access books and a quiet place to learn. That work sat inside a broader movement: Prashraya (Team Aashraya) publicly cites 400+ free libraries nationwide — scaled with district partnerships in places like Narsinghpur and Moradabad — plus learning centres and Aashraya Vidyalayas.

My role: volunteer/contributor supporting library efforts — not a personal library-count KPI.

Donation drives

I organized and took part in donation efforts — collecting and coordinating books, essentials, and relief materials. Context for the drives I joined: Aashraya/Prashraya’s COVID-19 nationwide book collection (~1,00,000 books with ~1,500 volunteers joining quickly), and Hamari Pahchan’s published 1,500+ COVID-19 kits.

My role: participant in drives — org kit/book totals are theirs, not personal tallies.

Fundraising campaigns

I hosted and supported fundraising campaigns for underprivileged children — including COVID-19 campaigns tied to book drives and relief kits — bringing people together and helping channel support toward education and welfare.

Timeline

Campaigns & timeline

Key org-documented moments that frame the volunteer work I took part in.

  1. 2015 onward

    Hamari Pahchan founded (Delhi)

    Founded by Tarun Mathur. Programs include Drishti (education), Sukhad (menstrual health), skill development, and later COVID response (corona kits + Gadgetshala). Published impact: 2,25,000+ children, 80,000+ women.

    Source: hamaripahchan.org

  2. 2019 → present

    Team Aashraya → Prashraya Welfare Foundation

    Founded 2019 in Tumda, Madhya Pradesh, by Priyanshu Khemariya as Team Aashraya; evolved into Prashraya. Focus: Shiksha, Shakti, Paryavaran, Chikitsa, Vastra. Public claims include 400+ free libraries, 35 learning centres, 9 Aashraya Vidyalayas (+ digital centre), 10,000+ volunteers, and 20+ states reach.

    Source: prashraya.org/about · prashraya.org/projects

  3. COVID-19 / lockdown era · ~2020–2021

    Nationwide book collection (Aashraya / Prashraya)

    Indian Masterminds (Oct 2021) reported ~1,00,000 books collected in days, with ~1,500 volunteers joining quickly; the drive expanded pan-India across ~25 states/UTs for rural libraries, schools, and orphanages. The team also contributed actively during COVID-19 across Shiksha, Chikitsa, and related pillars.

    Source: Indian Masterminds, Oct 2021 · prashraya.org

  4. COVID-19

    COVID relief kits (Hamari Pahchan)

    Hamari Pahchan’s public resources cite 1,500+ COVID-19 kits distributed, alongside broader resource programs (including menstrual kits framed at 50,000+ on the resources page).

    Source: hamaripahchan.org/resources/

  5. Ongoing

    Library expansion & education access

    Continued growth of free libraries and learning centres — including partnerships with district administrations (e.g. Narsinghpur & Moradabad). About-page language also cites 800+ libraries established/supported via district partnerships; this showcase prefers the primary 400+ free libraries figure from projects.

    Source: prashraya.org/projects · prashraya.org/about

Partners

Organizations

Background on the NGOs I’ve worked with. Numbers are from each organization’s public materials — organizational reach, not individual KPIs.

Prashraya Welfare Foundation

Formerly Team Aashraya / Aashraya

A youth-led Section 8 non-profit that began in 2019 as Team Aashraya in Tumda, Madhya Pradesh, and evolved into Prashraya Welfare Foundation. Focus areas: Shiksha, Shakti, Paryavaran, Chikitsa, and Vastra. Founded by Priyanshu Khemariya.

  • 400+ free libraries (primary; about also cites 800+ via partnerships)
  • 20+ states · book drive across ~25 states/UTs
  • 10,000+ volunteers
  • 35 learning centres · 9 Aashraya Vidyalayas (+ digital)
  • ~1,00,000 books in COVID-19 nationwide drive · ~1,500 volunteers joined quickly

Organizational claims from public materials — not personal metrics.

Visit prashraya.org →

Hamari Pahchan NGO

Delhi · founded 2015 · Tarun Mathur

A Delhi-based NGO working across education, skill development, hunger relief, menstrual health, and community programs. Flagship initiatives include Drishti (education), Sukhad (menstrual), skill development, and COVID response (corona kits + Gadgetshala).

  • 2,25,000+ children reached
  • 80,000+ women reached
  • 1,500+ COVID-19 kits
  • 50,000+ menstrual kits (resources-page framing)

Organizational claims from public materials — not personal metrics.

Thread

How this work connects

BooksSupportAccess

Libraries without books, or children without the means to stay in school, leave gaps that no single classroom can fill. My volunteer work — supporting libraries inside a 400+ free-library movement, organizing donations and COVID-19 drives, and hosting fundraising campaigns — was aimed at one thread: education access for underprivileged children.

Each activity feeds the next: spaces to learn, materials to fill them, and community support to keep those efforts alive. That’s the impact story I can own honestly — contribution alongside published org reach, not inflated certificates.
